question.text: Deepak, aged 55, has a single income and grown-up children. He has a conservative risk profile and Rs. 50,00,000 to invest. According to the model portfolio, how much should go into equities / diversified equity schemes?

explanation.text: The Logic: The model portfolio for the single-income / grown-up children / conservative profile allocates 35% to equities / diversified equity schemes. 35% of Rs. 50,00,000 = Rs. 17,50,000. The full source allocation is 35% equity (Rs. 17,50,000), 15% gold (Rs. 7,50,000), 10% gilt (Rs. 5,00,000), 20% debt (Rs. 10,00,000) and 20% liquid (Rs. 10,00,000). The Trap: Rs. 7,50,000 (Option B) is the gold line (15%). Rs. 25,00,000 (Option C) is 50%, which is the equity line in the young high-risk profile, not the conservative profile. Rs. 10,00,000 (Option D) matches either the debt or liquid line (20% each). Note: The arithmetic and allocation are taken directly from the source model portfolio table for this profile; this question tests percentage-to-rupee conversion against the correct line.
